stories.title: A database is a store for global variables
stories.summary: Databases are for storing global variables. We usually call them “rows” or “records” instead, but they’re definitionally global variables: any part of your program can read or write them. Isn’t this kind of weird? It’s common programming advice that global variables are bad, and yet many elegant programs rely on databases.

stories.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
stories.summary: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T via Pass@(K,T), we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten.

stories.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
stories.summary: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. Yet manipulation often hinges on precisely the visual signals most vulnerable to this abstraction, e.g., local geometry, boundaries, depth, and subtle state changes.

stories.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
stories.summary: Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.

stories.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
stories.summary: AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line.

stories.title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks
stories.summary: A frontier AI model is trained in an AI data center, on tens of thousands of accelerators joined by a dedicated network, and every training step ends with all of them exchanging data at once. Between racks, that network is optical, and each of its four layers, from lasers to switches, runs a fixed or after-the-fact policy. Lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can fail together.
